classification.classification_note: The benchmark metadata labels OSS-Fuzz issue 42527545 as CWE-457/use-of-uninitialized-value. The staged crash is a MemorySanitizer SEGV on a READ in `NflogTlv::assign()` after TLV traversal steps into padding with an underaligned stride; that read can reach uninitialized or past-end bytes.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42527545 (PcapPlusPlus): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target FuzzTarget [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42527545
bug_description.normalized: PcapPlusPlus advances NFLOG TLV iteration by the raw `recordLen` field even though NFLOG TLVs occupy 4-byte-aligned slots. `getNextTLVRecord()` can therefore call `NflogTlv::assign()` on a pointer into padding, and `assign()` immediately reads `*recordRawData` in its zero-skipping loop before any later cleanup can null the record. The staged witness reaches that path and produces the saved MemorySanitizer SEGV-on-READ.

source.code:
NflogTlv tlv = m_TlvReader.getTLVRecord(
		static_cast<uint32_t> (type),
		getTlvsBasePtr(),
		m_DataLen - sizeof(nflog_header));
source.description: First target-parser statement that consumes attacker-controlled NFLOG packet bytes as a TLV search space. It passes the raw TLV base pointer and logical TLV extent to the generic reader while requesting `NFULA_PAYLOAD`.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is exactly 167 bytes with sha256 `e8802aa1e02017b5bab4c6fd3ee097619fbc6e5eac4930f3497f8f05ddd634d5`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` writes those bytes verbatim to `/tmp/fuzz_sample.pcap`, opens them through `pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice`, reads the first packet into `pcpp::RawPacket rawPacket`, and constructs `pcpp::Packet parsedPacket(&rawPacket)`. The saved Stage 01 crash stack proves this packet then reaches `pcpp::Packet::setRawPacket()` and `pcpp::NflogLayer::parseNextLayer()` on the vulnerable run.

tainted_value_origin.description: First concrete vulnerability-relevant value. The current TLV's attacker-controlled `recordLen` is reinterpreted as the traversal stride for the next-record calculation.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `getTotalSize()` returns the raw NFLOG TLV length instead of the format's 4-byte-aligned record size, so later traversal can advance into padding rather than to the next TLV header.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this method to `align<4>(m_Data->recordLen)` and deletes the byte-by-byte zero-skip in `assign()`, showing that the missing obligation is to use aligned TLV sizes rather than probing through padding.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. `assign()` dereferences the candidate next-record pointer and keeps probing forward while the bytes are zero. When traversal entered padding instead of a real TLV header, one of these loop tests read beyond the valid TLV bytes and triggered the saved SEGV-on-READ.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: SEGV`, `The signal is caused by a READ memory access`, and pinpoints `assign /src/PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/header/NflogLayer.h:117:12`.

parser_admitted.condition: On the reproducing path the parsed packet's link type reaches `LINKTYPE_NFLOG`, because this is the only dispatch branch that can instantiate `NflogLayer` and lead to the saved stack `pcpp::NflogLayer::parseNextLayer -> getTlvByType -> getTLVRecord -> getNextTLVRecord -> assign`.

coarse_trace.summary: The parsed capture packet is admitted into the packet decoder, which reaches an `NflogLayer` and calls its `parseNextLayer()` method.
The NFLOG parser looks for the `NFULA_PAYLOAD` TLV inside the bytes after `nflog_header`.
The parser launches a TLV search over the attacker-controlled TLV span and requests a record of type `NFULA_PAYLOAD`.
The generic TLV reader materializes `curRec` from the TLV base pointer, finds that this record's type is not `NFULA_PAYLOAD`, and falls through to `getNextTLVRecord()`.

The next-record helper accepts the current record because `record_base + raw recordLen` still lies inside the TLV byte span, then calls `assign()` on `record_base + recordLen` even though that raw stride can stop in padding.
The TLV wrapper probes forward from that miscomputed pointer with `while (*recordRawData == 0)` and crashes on the read.

fine_trace.code:
NflogTlv tlv = m_TlvReader.getTLVRecord(
		static_cast<uint32_t> (type),
		getTlvsBasePtr(),
		m_DataLen - sizeof(nflog_header));
fine_trace.note: Source. After NFLOG dispatch, `parseNextLayer()` asks the TLV reader to search the attacker-controlled bytes after `nflog_header` for `NFULA_PAYLOAD`. This call fixes the TLV base pointer, TLV byte span, and requested type used by the later traversal.

`getTLVRecord()` materializes the current TLV wrapper from the attacker-controlled TLV base pointer. On the crashing path, `getFirstTLVRecord()` returns a non-null `curRec` whose `m_Data` points at the current TLV header bytes, so later `getType()`, `getRecordBasePtr()`, and `getTotalSize()` all read from this attacker-chosen record.

Root cause and tainted value origin. On `curRec`, `getTotalSize()` returns the attacker's raw `recordLen` instead of the NFLOG TLV's 4-byte-aligned slot size. That raw value becomes the stride for later traversal and can undercount the padded footprint. The fix replaces this with `align<4>(m_Data->recordLen)`.

The current TLV's type does not match the requested `NFULA_PAYLOAD`, so this comparison is false on the crashing iteration. Control therefore reaches line 321 and asks `getNextTLVRecord()` to advance from the current record.

In the staged vulnerable checkout, the next-record helper reaches the pre-assign checks at lines 288-294. On the crashing iteration, the record is non-null, its base pointer is not below `tlvDataBasePtr`, and this line-293 guard also passes because it validates only that `record_base + raw recordLen` stays inside `tlvDataLen`. It does not require the full 4-byte-aligned TLV slot to fit and does not account for the later zero-skip read in `assign()`.

Line 296 computes the candidate next-record pointer by adding the raw `recordLen` from step 3 to the current record base pointer from step 2. Because that stride ignores NFLOG's 4-byte alignment, the resulting address can begin in padding instead of on the next TLV header. `assign()` is called on that pointer before the later `if (resRec.getTotalSize() == 0) resRec.assign(NULL);` cleanup can run.

Sink. `assign()` dereferences the candidate pointer from step 6 in `while (*recordRawData == 0)` and scans forward over zero bytes while looking for a TLV header. On the witnessed path, one of these reads performs the crashing READ reported in `sanitizer_trace.txt` at `Packet++/header/NflogLayer.h:117:12`, so the caller's post-assign cleanup never executes first.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The reproduced MSan stack matches the same function chain and sink code. Its line numbers come from the staged runnable checkout at later vulnerable commit `f4e873e493b87fbc1bbc5f40065a2bbcc2437f35`, where the same `TLVData.h` statements appear at lines 296 and 321 instead of 291 and 319 in metadata vulnerable commit `843765f594a3d0c494c2c64e5c2b786f02122ccc`.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: Stage 01 did not run the fixed build, so `patch_resolves` remains false here. Source-grounded inspection of `patch.diff` nevertheless matches the traced mechanism: the fix aligns NFLOG TLV sizes to 4 bytes and removes the zero-skipping probe in `assign()`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42527545 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `MemorySanitizer: SEGV`, identified the access as a READ, and matched the stack `assign -> getNextTLVRecord -> getTLVRecord -> getTlvByType -> pcpp::NflogLayer::parseNextLayer -> pcpp::Packet::setRawPacket`.

format.name: staged NFLOG-in-PCAP witness file
format.contract: Exactly the staged 167-byte witness file `poc` with sha256 `e8802aa1e02017b5bab4c6fd3ee097619fbc6e5eac4930f3497f8f05ddd634d5`. The staged artifacts prove only this exact witness. On the reproducing path, `PcapFileReaderDevice` accepts it, the first parsed packet is dispatched into `NflogLayer`, and `parseNextLayer()` searches the TLV bytes after `nflog_header` for `NFULA_PAYLOAD`. During that search, the current TLV's raw `recordLen` is used as the next-record stride, `getNextTLVRecord()` calls `assign()` on a pointer that begins in padding, and `assign()` crashes while testing `*recordRawData`. The patch and source show this depends on a TLV whose raw length is smaller than its 4-byte-aligned footprint, but the staged evidence does not establish any broader trigger family beyond this exact witness and parser state.
